name: The Smiths
hook: A Manchester band whose guitarist learned from Nile Rodgers and Phil Spector, and whose singer's picture of bleak urban England fed Britpop.
blurb: The Smiths formed in Manchester in 1982: Morrissey sang and wrote the words, Johnny Marr played guitar and wrote the music, with Andy Rourke on bass and Mike Joyce on drums. They signed to Rough Trade, an independent label, in 1983 and split up in 1987, amid tension between the two writers. Marr's guitar parts ring and sparkle instead of chugging. He has named Nile Rodgers of Chic, Bert Jansch, James Williamson and James Honeyman-Scott as influences, and said he wanted records to sound symphonic, the whole band merged into one atmosphere, an idea he took from Phil Spector. Morrissey's songs about dull, rainy English towns and loneliness were a big influence on the Britpop bands of the 1990s: Wikipedia names Oasis, Blur and Suede, and Noel Gallagher has called Marr unique and borrowed his guitars. Marr went on to form Electronic with Bernard Sumner of New Order. In 2017 Morrissey said the UKIP leadership election had been rigged against the anti-Islam activist Anne Marie Waters. In 2018 he backed her far-right British party, For Britain, and in 2019 he wore its badge on stage in New York, while saying he despised racism. Adverts for his album were taken down from Merseyrail stations, some shops refused to stock it, and Billy Bragg said he was dragging the Smiths' legacy through the dirt. Many people now argue about whether that changes how they hear the Smiths.

signatureTracks.title: This Charming Man
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Marr's bright, ringing guitar lines at their most recognisable.

signatureTracks.title: How Soon Is Now?
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A slow, swamping tremolo guitar sound, built in the studio layer by layer.

signatureTracks.title: There Is a Light That Never Goes Out
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Morrissey's lonely, funny, doomed England, with strings.
